title: Von Neumann Algebra Automorphisms and Time-Thermodynamics Relation in General Covariant Quantum Theories
version: arXiv:gr-qc/9406019v1 (HTML v1); Class. Quantum Grav. 11 (1994) 2899-2917 (journal locator from existing frontier record and Hersent's reference list, which gives vol 11, 1994, DOI 10.1088/0264-9381/11/12/007; pages not re-verified)
locators: Sec. 2.1 eqs. (6)-(8) modular objects and flow; Sec. 3.1 thermal time hypothesis and KMS eqs. (21)-(23); Sec. 4.1 Gibbs case eqs. (29)-(44); Sec. 4.2 formal classical limit eqs. (45)-(50); Sec. 4.3 Unruh/Bisognano-Wichmann eqs. (55)-(57); second Sec. 4.3 outer-automorphism class. Locators come from a retrieval-summarizer pass over the HTML, not a verbatim transcription; spot-check equation numbers before citing.
assumptions: Von Neumann algebra R with cyclic separating vector (or faithful state on a C*-algebra via GNS). Hypothesis: physical time is the modular flow of the state; temperature is the ratio of thermal to geometric time.
conclusion: Paper authors' claim: the thermal time hypothesis is a postulate supported by consequences: Gibbs case gives alpha_t = gamma_{beta t} (derived); Hamilton equations recovered formally in a classical limit (heuristic); Unruh temperature via Bisognano-Wichmann (derivation from a cited theorem). Cited established results: Tomita-Takesaki theorem, Connes cocycle theorem (state-dependence only up to inner automorphisms, canonical flow on Out(R)), HHW KMS-Gibbs equivalence.
proof_status: Postulate, not theorem; cited theorems not re-proved here; formal classical limit is heuristic by the paper's own account.
dependencies: Tomita-Takesaki modular theory; Connes cocycle theorem; KMS condition; Haag-Hugenholtz-Winnink; Bisognano-Wichmann for Unruh case.
open_questions: What bridge premise turns a modular flow (a one-parameter automorphism group) into time that a physical clock registers? Which state is 'the' thermal state of a generally covariant universe? How does state-dependence of the flow square with an objective ontology of time?
relevance: Anchor for 'state-defined flow'. Supersedes the abstract-depth phil-thermal-time and the locator-poor frontier record by adding locators; does not replace them.
limits: Read via retrieval summarizer over HTML v1 (small-model extraction), not by direct line reading; proofs of cited theorems not audited; no empirical test in the paper. Thermal-time hypothesis is the authors' proposal.

title: Thermal time of noncommutative Minkowski spacetime
version: arXiv:2502.12750v1 [hep-th], submitted 18 Feb 2025 (self-described preliminary version); a later arXiv version was not checked
locators: Sec. 2.1-2.4 (algebra A_l, weight omega eq. (5), modular function, twisted cyclicity eq. (13)); Sec. 3.2 (omega not normalisable, modular operator = I^2); Sec. 4.1 kappa-Minkowski eq. (21)-(22); Sec. 4.2 thermal Hamiltonian and lack of kappa-Poincare invariance; Sec. 4.3 rho-Minkowski; Sec. 5.2-5.3 phenomenology and open issues. Characters 100000-116898 of the HTML text (end of references) not read by me; the dead GLM worker's log shows it read Secs. 3-5 and the reference list directly.
assumptions: Deformed Minkowski algebra as Hopf dual of deformed translation algebra; weight = spacetime integral (infinite on identity, hence not a state); twist given by the modular function of the momentum group; thermal time hypothesis applied to a weight rather than a normalised state.
conclusion: Paper author's claims: for kappa-Minkowski the modular flow is a shift of global time x0 by (d/kappa)t (thermal Hamiltonian (d/kappa)p0), with kappa read as a temperature scale and omega a 'highest temperature' state; for rho-Minkowski the group is unimodular, the twist is trivial and the flow is trivial, linked to discreteness of global time. Flow selects a preferred frame (not kappa-Poincare invariant). Phenomenology (Sec. 5.2) is speculative.
proof_status: Formal-power-series level; the author states the full C*-algebra structure is not constructed and inner-automorphism freedom is left open. Not independently checked by me.
dependencies: Connes-Rovelli thermal time hypothesis; Tomita-Takesaki theory extended to weights; Matassa 2013 (arXiv:1212.3462) and Poulain-Wallet 2018 (arXiv:1801.02715) cited as modular/KMS-weight predecessors (cited in Hersent's reference list per worker log; not read by anyone in this lane).
open_questions: Is the thermal time of a non-normalisable tracial weight a clock for any observer? Does the twist survive a proper C*-completion? Does choosing a different weight change the flow beyond inner automorphisms?
relevance: Anchor for 'mathematical flow equals a coordinate translation by construction'; no operational clock is described.
limits: Preprint v1, self-described preliminary; read through a retrieval summarizer; partly read by me, whole by the dead worker (log only). Not peer-review evidence.
